To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the prevalence of HPV infection is not significantly increased in HIV-infected women; 2) the incidence of HPV infection and high-risk types was high in this group, suggesting a need for early vaccination; and 3) cytologic abnormalities were common, and progression to high grade lesions was frequent.

HPV prevalence is similar between HIV-infected and uninfected women in early childhood, but the incidence of new HPV infections is higher among HIV-infected individuals, and HPV vaccination should be strongly considered for HIV-infected women.
HPV infection is common in Romanian women infected during early childhood with HIV, and the rate of Pap smears abnormalities is high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the prevalence of cervical HPV infection in a cohort of Romanian women with HIV infection during early childhood.
the study of the prevalence of HPV infection and its association with the immune status of HIV-positive women.
the epidemiology of HPV infection in HIV-infected women and its relationship with cytologic abnormalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HPV infection is a common problem in HIV-infected Romanian women, and that the risk for progression to cytologic abnormalities is high.
HPV infection in Romanian HIV-infected women is common, but the incidence rate of HPV acquisition is low.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of HPV infection is similar in Romanian women infected during early childhood with HIV and uninfected controls.
the prevalence of HPV is not significantly higher in HIV-infected women in Romania than in controls.
the prevalence of HPV infection in HIV-infected women is similar to that of controls, and the incidence of HPV acquisition is similar to other studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HPV infection in HIV-infected women is common and that the rate of cytologic progression is much higher than in the general population.
HPV vaccination should be offered to all HIV-infected women.
